committee_name.text: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee

quote.quote: Durezol (difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion) 0.05% was presented before the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee on May 29, 2008. The Committee voted in favor of approval.
An advisory committee meeting was held on May 29, 2008. The committee concurred with the potential approval of the application and raised no new issues of safety or efficacy.

recommendation.text: The committee voted in favor of approval; the consensus was that difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion should be approved for the treatment of ocular inflammation and pain associated with ocular surgery, and the committee raised no new issues of safety or efficacy.

quote.quote: The consensus of the advisory committee meeting was that difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion should be approved for the treatment of ocular inflammation and pain associated with ocular surgery.

summary: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met on May 29, 2008 because difluprednate is a new molecular entity, and voted in favor of approval of Durezol for ocular inflammation and pain associated with ocular surgery, raising no new issues of safety or efficacy. The only specific question recorded (a committee member asking whether difluprednate was effective in subjects with concomitant pain and inflammation) prompted an additional analysis that demonstrated statistically significant differences versus vehicle, supporting the existing efficacy claim rather than causing any change. The review documents describe no AdComm-driven change to the label, indication, dosing, or postmarketing requirements.
